¶3 I think the first 20 page is theoretical and then practical Irfan.

¶4 okay, how an Aarif would start building their soul in a way to prepare it to receive the favors and blessings of Allah(swt). Of course, Inshallah, we will talk about sulook but right now we will talk about practical advice, but the more practical side of it is sulook that is actually moving towards Allah (swt) and will mention that the whole effort is to remove the veils which are covering the hearts and of course, it's not easy therefore, different mystics, different Aarifs, they have improvised different methods, and that's how the tariqas have appeared, Sufi tariqa as the Sufi orders so to speak, have appeared. But the basic principle is the same thing they use different methods just to remove that veil, which is covering the heart and wouldn't let it to see the glory of Allah (swt) and to feel the presence.

¶5 Now, how this is possible, of course the elements of mysticism in all mystical traditions whether Islamic, non Islamic is the same, again when we come to sulook you would find that there are five major concepts which are prevailing in all mystical traditions, of course, how to qualify them then would make us a Muslim mystic or a Christian mystic, or Buddhist mystic, but the main elements are similar. Now you will see here I want to quote someone, a Christian mystic, the story of Nestorian church which was which is now a very, very small church, perhaps even non existent it was the Church of the eastern part of Christianity in the old times, some parts of them live in Iran now.

¶6 I think Armenians are a bit close to the Nestorian, Isaac of Nineveh of the seventh century was an eastern mystic, and he mentioned a few things about how mystics, orafas setting out towards the journey towards the God, he said that human being consists of body the lower soul, which is nafs and the higher soul, which is ruhh, this is a good analysis, of course, I mean, if you want to analyze our own selves, we know that we have a body and inshallah we know that we have a soul. And the soul is consists of two sides, one which is all the time attending the bodily affairs, which is the lower soul and one which is facing upwards towards Allah (swt) and is longing for spirituality, which is the higher soul of course, we have different names for it.

¶7 You call them Nafsul ammarah, Nafsul mutmainnah, but it's all different aspects of the same thing. Then he said, of course, the path of mysticism consists of after we have analyzed this, he says that to remove the veils from the heart, we have to purify all these three aspects of our existence, body, the lower soul which manages the body and the higher soul which receive blessings from Allah (swt). And of course, purification should encompass all these three aspects of our existence because we want to go towards the purest of the pure towards Allah (swt). If you want to move towards him, you have to purify everything you have to clean everything because dirt and filth cannot enter into that threshold.

¶8 Now, to purify the body we have to repent from our sins. So first of all, the first step, which of course most older mystics would mention is repentance, repentance, of course, not only from the sin, but from whatever we usually casually do in our life, which is offensive, when we think about it, offensive in with regards to Allah(swt). Then, of course, the lower soul should be purified, which I will explain shortly. And the higher soul of course the higher soul ruhh is pure, the ruhh cannot be polluted. The only thing is that when we are polluted, the ruhh doesn't exist anymore, it is taken away when the ruhh is there it is pure, however it needs perception, it needs growth, it needs development.

¶9 So the body is purified to repentance, the lower soul to purification and the higher soul through perfection. Now repentance as he explains it, Isaac of Nainevah explains it. This is why I have mentioned him because he's very close to our mystics. His fahm, his understanding the Nestorian church was the church which believed that Jesus was not Son of God. So they were closer to our ideas, he says that repentance are works of righteousness performed with the body like fasting, nice rituals, alms giving whatever actually you do with your body in terms of good intention and in terms of intending to go closer to Allah (swt) these are all the aspects which go back to repentance you have to repent if you have not fasted, you have to fast you have to repent if you have not given charity, you have to give charity and so on and so forth.

¶10 Purification are the virtues of lower soul, like neighborly love, humility for peers, whatever comes in to the heart, rather than bodily having bodily appearance, and of course perfection are gifts bestowed by God like the light, exaltation and love which you do not do anything for them, after you purify your lower soul they come from Allah (swt). If you remember we said love of God is something which would come into your heart you cannot create it yourself. It is something that after you have purified yourself, it would be placed there by Allah (swt), so perfection of the soul is the work the acts of God according to Isaac Nainavah. Now let's see how Muslim mystics put these into their own terminology.

¶11 Of course, this is very crude and large preliminary type of study of practical Irfan when we go to Islamic site of mysticism you find that they have made all these more developed, they have expanded all these ideas and in terms of practice, of course their practices are more consistent than other mystics. Now in Islamic mysticism, they say you have four steps to reach the peak of the practise, which ends the first journey of your soul this is now we take the soul has forge in mystical travel and of course the first journey has four stations which ends in Sana……(11:15)…. and when the soul is anihilated of course, we will explain what this means that the soul is anihilated then you have stopped you have finished the first journey and you have to start the second journey which is of course, much more wonderful and amusing than this first journey of the mystics, now we'll talk about that later on.

¶12 The first journey consists of tajliyyah, which is furbishing polishing making something shiny and that is of course, you polish your body and your lower soul. Now this tajliyyah would correspond with what Isaac of Nineveh called repentance. And then it's takhliyyah abandoning or it's also called tarkhiyyah to purify, this corresponds to purification ofcourse of Isaac of Naineveh then this tahliyyah adorning that is that corresponds to perfection that's Isaac of Naineveh was mentioning. The ruhh gets affected by this tahliyyah, and then anhilation is something which of course he did not mention, and it is very, very important in Islamic mysticism. And probably this is a characteristic of Islamic mysticism. Of course, we can compare it with some other concepts in other mystical tradition, but certainly it's not the same as what they other school say, we'll examine this shortly, now what is tajliyyah, is to furbish the soul and the body whatever the Prophet orders for us to do in terms of wajibat , in terms of mustahabaat as in terms of avoidance from whatever is haram and whatever is makrooh so the first step in mystical journey is that you try to stick to the Quran and the Sunnah of the Prophet, in the most in the strictest sense of the verse.

¶13 And we have many, many verses in the Quran of course, talking about the seriousness of the way that you could take whatever is said in the book in a serious way or in a casual. For example, with regards to banu Israiil we have the verse khuzoo maaa aatainaakum biquwwatinw(sura2:ayat 93), take whatever we have given you with a strength, in a strength means that take it serious and do your best to comply with whatever is mentioned. For the order which comes for Prophet Yahya ‘Yaa Yahyaa khuzil Kitaaba biquwwatinw wa aatainaahul hukma sabiyyaa’(sura19:ayat12), Oh Yahya take the book with a strength. With a strength means that well, of course you have to understand deeply and practice it, in especially in shiah mysticism the shia mystics say that unless you have furbished your soul and your body with whatever sharia said you cannot move to the next step.

¶14 And this is very important for those who want to begin this journey because usually, when we want to begin this journey, we say okay, who is going to guide us who's going to instruct us and we will look for a teacher, for instructor for a mentor to tell us what to do and what not to do and if we do not find it, find him or her then we say okay, we don't have a teacher we cannot set out on this journey. However, this teacher could not be found, unless you have somehow moved away from these preliminary things towards more deeper aspects of Irfan. So, if you want a teacher or a mentor, instructing the beginning of the way is not the one you need.

¶15 First you have to comply completely with whatever Sharia tells. And of course, there are some other issues, extra issues which are mentioned in Sharia, in Hadith, which ordinary people are not ordered to do and for someone who wants to go through this path, they have to do them as well. However, of course, we need a teacher in the sense to tell us okay, which hadith is important to act according to it or which hadith, is very instrumental in the beginning of the way. Well we have in a very famous Hadith, this is a very authentic Hadees that Prophet (pbuh) used to recite al Musabbihaat every night before he used to sleep, al musabbihaat are the five Surahs which start with sabbahaa , it starts with Surah Hadid 57 and then Surah Hashr 59 and then 61 Surah Saff and then Surah Juma and surah Taghabun.

¶16 And of course, some people say Surah Sabbihisma Rabbikal A'laa(sura86) sabbaha , of course, this is not a part of Musabbihaat but some people say it's important that you recite that as well, however Holy Prophet used to recite that as well. Now, of course, this is a hadith if you go to Kaafi, you will find it there. But not most people would, would act according to this practice this hadith. It's difficult to recite all these six surahs every night before we sleep. Now, you need a teacher in the sense that the teacher will tell you what this is important. If you want to set out on this journey this is important, Allama Tabatabaii (ra) had a teacher Syed Ali Qadhi Tabrizi, who was a wonderful man in this mystical tradition, and he used whenever he wanted to instruct beginners to set out on this journey, he emphasized that they have to recite these Surahs before they sleep for one year before he gave them the second instruction.

¶17 So it's a very gradual path, I think we have discussed about this earlier. Now, this record in…(19:40)… and Imam Jafare Sadiq (as) says that it is compulsory in the sense for those who want to set out on a deeper understanding of religion and Irfani type of understanding it is compulsory in fiqh for them to do otherwise it's not compulsory in terms of fiqh. Because then if it was compulsory in terms of fiqh it would have been in Tauziul Masaael risalat that you have to say this zikr every morning and every evening.

¶22 Now then after a person has done this, then gradually succeed for takhliyyah, means you remove whatever is in the heart. He says, the beginning of Irfan, is tafreequn wa nafsun tarqun, it is separation, dusting of abandonment and rejection.

¶23 These four steps are different levels of takhliyah, separation is separation within the Knower and whatever diversing from God, so if you love anything against the love of God, we may love many things which would not contradict with love of God at all. This is the first step of takhliyah, the devices of the heart of course, are more difficult to remove from devices of the body. You can very easily very easily abstain from drinking wine or abstain from meeting people.

¶24 However, it's very difficult to abstain from thinking evil about other people or from having completely being occupied with something which will let you away takes you away from forceful prayer was when we pray you see how difficult it is to remove all other thoughts except the thoughts about Allah (swt) so we have to separate our hearts from whatever was diverted from God. Now, then he said, Okay, with fanaa, we don't know really what mystics mean when they say annihilation, it is the lower soul as our system mentioned, man's attributes man, entire individual as some mystics say, or mans personality, and then he says, if so, it is not clear what would survive God alone or man with God's attributes or man as an original idea, in the mind of God.

¶53 Now, this last one is very difficult to understand man as an original idea in the mind of God. However this shows that there is a confusion here in the mind of an Orientalist like him who has actually searched through the mystical book and haven't found what's really fanaa. But we have another Orientalist who, who has really found out because if you go to mystical books it is so clear, the books on fanaa, what they mean by fanaa, and what is annihilation that they need. He says that this is an example of Alexander Kynsh, in his book Islamic mysticism. He says that there are two complimentary definitions of fanaa, one is passing away of all things from the consciousness of the mystic include including self perception, this experiential vacuum is filled by pure consciousness of God that secludes any perception of others.

¶54 I think this is a very instrumental definition of fanaa, it shows to great extents what really the mystics mean when they talk about fanaa, they don't say that the individuals would annihilate, and mystic who was actually recently patient of fanaa, they are here in front of us. Of course, they are not…. Well, if the body is there, how do you say that the soul is destroyed while the soul the body is managed by the soul of the mystic, and when we talk about annihilation of the soul of the mystic, we are not talking about some sort of imaginary world, we are talking about this very world. So they sit in front of us and they say that we have arrived at the station of fanaa, now what that means is that they encounter a glory, actually, this is the highest faith of tahliyah, as I said, God would give them a light by which they see things that other people don't see, when they see things are completely conscious of themselves.

¶55 Okay, now, then, at the end of this, God would show them his own glory of course, at a very low level, very superficial. God would show them His glory, and when they see that glory, they lose their self consciousness, the sense of self perception they lose, they cannot see both God and themselves. It's like for example, when you're thrilled to a very great extent, you just forget many things which are going around you and even if, for example, you cut your hand or your foot or you have a very bad injury, you cannot think about you do not see because you are faced with something very frightening or very, very pleasurable or something like that you lose your sense the sense of your body.

¶56 Now, these mystics were at the highest stages of Tahliyah, adorning on the soul. When Allah (swt) shows them His glory, they cannot both watch that glory and have a sense of self perception. So they lose the sense of self perception, now if you lose the sense of self perception, you have no selfishness of course of one it is completely obvious. There are no we have no self anymore, not that you have no self that you have no soul, you cannot think about it. You have no perception. And this is when they say we have come to this station of fanaa annihilation, the soul is there everything is there, what they lose is the sense of selfishness because they encounter the glory of Allah (swt), and of course this is a talk that we are actually exchanging we will not know what type of experiences they have talked about this experience, and they have written in their books, what this experience is like, but of course it's just like if you want to say what's the experience of a specific type of fragrance, you never can explain.

¶57 It's impossible, especially if you don't have anything similar to that to simulate or to compare it with. So there is no human experience comparable to this. So the mystics cannot say what is it like? They just can't say that they lose self perception, and they cannot think about themselves anymore. So, tapping away all things from the consciousness of the mystic, including self perception and this experiential vacuum is filled by pure consciousness of God that precludes any perception of others. Now, of course, the process is, is in the reverse order. In fact, the consciousness of Gods when it comes, it takes everything away rather than first creating a vacuum and then consciousness of God comes into, no consciousness of God comes and everything else would go away even the self perception.

¶58 Now, then, the second definition of fanaa which he mentions in his book is, falling away of the imperfect attributes of this fallible creature as a replacement by the perfect attributes of the Divine Self. Now, he says complimentary, actually, they are the same thing. After you have completely moved during perfect imperfect attributes, you could only see the glory of God and when you see that glory his attributes actually penetrate into soul. So they are complimentary they are if you want to take it to extreme identical thing. You see God's attributes, you don’t see your attributes anymore, you see God you don't see yourself anymore. And this is how fanaa starts, of course, fanaa has stages itself, but it starts to somehow come into the consciousness of the mystic.

¶59 In other words, fanaa is the annihilation of self perception of the mystics in perceiving the unveiling the reality of God, this is what the so called the glory of God. The unveiling of reality of God of course, when you say unveil, just where it can be. There are some veils between Allah and his creation which never go away, otherwise the creation would go away, even between the prophet and God, some ways, comparatively, the outer veils, which is between God and creation, it will go away, and therefore it would give the station of fanaa to the mystics and the annihilation of human characteristics of the mystics that will pave the way for attaining the attributes of God.

¶60 Now nirvana of Buddhists is also a type of fanaa that they talk about they say we want to arrive at nirvana. Now Knysh rightly mentioned that, unlike Nirvana with which fanaa is often compared in western studies of Sufism, these definitions of fanaa are presented not as a mere cessation of individual experience, but as the development of a more ample and perfect selfhood, and this is very correct. In fact, that human beings human existence expands in a way that it could wash the glory of Allah (swt). So it leaves an imperfect self for perfect self and more expanded one that is adorned by divine presence and fanaa should never be construed as a fusion of divine and human essence this is impossible, this is just a shirk or kufr.

¶61 If someone says that I am now dissolved in God or God is incarnated in me, these are just things which people are people with lack of understanding would say. So fanaa should never be construed as a fusion of divine and human essence, which was seen as the root of the erroneous doctrine of incarnation in Christianity and in many others. Hinduism for example, is a misunderstanding of this concept of fanaa, it seems that this concept of fanaa or this type of experience human experience has existed, right from the beginning of human creations, and in many false religions have come about because people did not understand what fanaa is and when they came to this station of fanaa, they actually confused themselves with God.
